⚠ Use at your own risk

These messages change how your Lumatone works at a low level. Wrong values can leave keys unplayable or make the keyboard inoperable. Changing settings with SysEx messages voids your warranty, and Lumatone technical support is not available for keyboards whose function has been damaged by changing these settings. Before you start, save your presets with Lumatone Editor.

If your Lumatone stops working properly

  1. Restore the default settings. Send Reset Board Thresholds (34h), Reset Aftertouch Trigger Delay (4Ch) and Reset Lumatouch Note Off Delay (4Dh) to each board (board IDs 01h to 05h). Then send Reset Velocity Configuration (0Ah), Reset Fader Configuration (0Dh), Reset Aftertouch Configuration (12h), Reset LumaTouch Configuration (2Fh), Reset Pitch and Modulation Wheel Thresholds (36h), Reset Expression Pedal Bounds (39h) and Reset Macro Light Intensity Settings (4Ah) to the main controller (board ID 00h).
  2. Recalibrate. In Lumatone Editor, open Settings and calibrate the keys, the aftertouch and the pitch and mod wheels. Without a computer, hold down both preset buttons on a board while powering up to calibrate that board's keys.
  3. Restore your presets. Load the presets you saved, or reset the presets to factory default in Lumatone Editor's Settings.
  4. Reinstall the latest firmware from the Software Downloads page.

intro.title: Message format
intro.html:
System Exclusive (SYSEX) messages are used to change operating parameters of the keyboard.

Each transmission message starts with the same four bytes. The first byte is a MIDI standard byte that indicates the start of a SYSEX transmission. The next three bytes are reserved for a manufacturer ID.

In general, each SYSEX transmission message follows the format shown in the table below.

SYSEX Message Format
BYTE 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 … 7+N 7+N+1
DESC

START

SYSEX

 Mfg ID1 Mfg ID2 Mfg ID3 BOARD ID CMD DATA1 DATA2 …

DATA

N

END

SYSEX
VALUE F0 00 21 50 00-05 00-7F 00-7F 00-7F 00-7F 00-7F F7
Start SYSEX Byte 0 is always value F0h to indicate the start of a SYSEX message.
Mfg. ID1, ID2, ID3 The manufacturer ID: Lumatone uses 00h 21h 50h.
BOARD ID

The specific board ID for which the SYSEX message is destined. Value can be 0-5.

  • 0 = main controller (the whole keyboard).

  • 1 = board 1, or the left-most board.

  • 2 = board 2.

  • 3 = board 3.

  • 4 = board 4.

  • 5 = board 5.
CMD The specific SYSEX command byte, from 00h-7Fh.
DATA1 to DATA N Data specific to the given CMD byte. There will always be a minimum of 4 DATA bytes
END SYSEX The last byte is always value F7h to indicate the end of the SYSEX message.

Note that all transactions are initiated via a command from the configuration application; with new commands only being issued after the response from the previous command has been received. The response SYSEX message is covered in Responses.

intro.title: Responses
intro.html:
Once the keyboard receives a SYSEX message, it will send back a response message once the SYSEX has been fully processed. If a SYSEX message is received during processing, it will respond with a busy response byte. The general format of the response SYSEX message is as follows.

SYSEX Message Format
BYTE 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 6+N 6+N+1
DESC

START

SYSEX

 Mfg ID1 Mfg ID2 Mfg ID3 BOARD ID CMD RESP DATA1 …

DATA

N

END

SYSEX
VALUE F0 00 21 50 00-05 00-7F 00-04 00-7F 00-7F 00-7F F7

The format of the SYSEX message is the same as the transmitted message with the inclusion of the response status byte located after the command byte. The response status byte ranges from 0x00 to 0x04:

  • 00h – NACK. The transmitted command was not recognized

  • 01h – ACK. The transmitted command was processed successfully

  • 02h – BUSY. The transmitted command was not processed as it is currently processing the previous transmitted message.

  • 03h – ERROR. The transmitted command was not processed due to invalid data or board ID byte parameters or message length.

  • 04h – STATE. The transmitted command was not processed due to the keyboard not being in the correct operating state. See Calibrate Aftertouch (0Fh), Calibrate Keys (24h) and Demo Mode (25h).

  • 04h – LIST FULL (deprecated in rev 1.4). This response message’s usage has been deprecated in version 1.4. Used exclusively by command 00h, it indicated that the transmitted data was not processed due to the maximum amount of faders configurable has been reached. More information: Set Key Parameters (00h).

The data bytes for the response message are dependent on the specific command transmitted.

cmds.name: Set Key Parameters
cmds.html:
This command is used to configure a specific key’s note, channel, and type parameters.

In firmware version 1.3, the response returns 04h if the maximum amount of faders has already been reached. The maximum amount of faders for the keyboard is 15 faders. If this scenario occurs, one of the faders on the keyboard must first be assigned back to a note first to decrement the internal fader list index. To determine the keyboard’s current key type setup, the command Get Type Configuration (0x18h) can be used to read the key set up. More information regarding this command is in Get Type Configuration (18h).

In document version 1.4, response packet 04h has been deprecated since fader polyphony limitations are performed on the go rather than a static maximum limit.

In firmware version 1.0.11 (documentation version 1.13), an extra key type was included: 00h Key Disabled.

Software variables affected include the following:

  • Key Channel values

  • Key Note or CC values

  • Key operating type

  • CC polarity values

The data array is composed of 127 12-bit variables which are used to map a range of time to a region index. Each increment of this velocity interval value represents ~1.1ms. extra.title: Peripheral Calibration Data (3Eh)
extra.html:
When the keyboard is performing calibration for the expression pedal or the pitch and modulation wheels, the Peripheral Calibration Data SYSEX message is sent from the keyboard roughly every 100ms. The format of the response SYSEX message is as follows:

SYSEX Message Format
BYTE 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7-21 22
DESC

START

SYSEX

 Mfg ID1 Mfg ID2 Mfg ID3 BOARD ID CMD MODE PAYLOAD

END

SYSEX
VALUE F0 00 21 50 00 3E 00-01 00-7F F7
Start SYSEX Byte 0 is always value F0h to indicate the start of a SYSEX message.
Mfg. ID1, ID2, ID3 The manufacturer ID: Lumatone uses 00h 21h 50h.
BOARD ID The peripheral calibration message will always output with board ID 0x00.
CMD SYSEX command byte 0x3E, Peripheral Calibration Data
MODE

The Mode field indicates which type of calibration the keyboard, and the message, is currently in.

  • 00h: Expression Pedal Calibration

  • 01h: Pitch and Modulation Wheel Calibration
PAYLOAD This message will always contain a payload size of 15, regardless of which calibration mode the keyboard is currently in.
END SYSEX The last byte is always value F7h to indicate the end of the SYSEX message.

Expression Pedal Calibration Status Payload

When the keyboard is currently in expression pedal calibration, it will output the peripheral calibration SYSEX message, with its mode field set to 00h.

The payload of the message during this mode is configured as the following:

PERIPHERAL CALIBRATION DATA SYSEX MESSAGE PAYLOAD
Byte Field Bit Range (hex) Notes:
0 Min bound 00-0Fh Bits 11-8 of the raw minimum ADC value
1 Min bound 00-0Fh Bits 7-4 of the raw ADC value
2 Min bound 00-0Fh Bits 3-0 of the raw ADC value
3 Max bound 00-0Fh Bits 11-8 of the raw ADC value
4 Max bound 00-0Fh Bits 7-4 of the raw ADC value
5 Max bound 00-0Fh Bits 3-0 of the raw ADC value
6 Valid 00h,01h Boolean indicating whether or not the expression pedal has been unplugged during any point of the calibration process. If it has been unplugged, this field will be written as 00h. Otherwise, the field will be written as 01h. Note that if the expression pedal was unplugged at any point during the calibration, the calibration values will be ignored at the end of the calibration routine.
7-14 -- XX

Expression Pedal Calibration Status Payload

When the keyboard is currently in pitch and modulation wheel calibration, it will output the peripheral calibration SYSEX message, with its mode field set to 01h.

extra.title: Velocity Curve Mapping
extra.html:
The Lumatone keyboard uses a time of flight methodology to determine the velocity instead of the conventional pressure sensor. Each board scans the ADC positioning of all its keys every 1.1 milliseconds. The board records how many intervals the key takes to travel between key release and depressed events. This is known as dwell ticks.

The Lumatone keyboard uses two data arrays, the velocity look up table and the velocity interval table, to map the dwell ticks to the final midi output velocity during a Note event. These tables can be configured via the SYSEX commands 0x08h and 0x20h.

When a Note event is being processed, the tick value is compared to the velocity interval table. The velocity interval table is a 127 12-bit array which determines the region where the dwell tick lies. Each 12-bit represents the maximum time of each region. Interval [0] represents the first node above 0ms while Interval [126] represents the last node before the maximum ticks which is 2048. Note that the data in the array must be configured with each such that index 0 contains the lowest amount of ticks and subsequent increments should be continue to be a greater value than the previous up to a number of 2047. A graphical representation of the velocity interval table is shown in Figure 1.

Figure 1: Graphical Representation of the Velocity Interval Array

Once the region index has been obtained from the velocity interval table, the region index is then put into the velocity look up table to obtain the final midi output value. A graphical representation of the velocity look up table is shown in Figure 2.

Figure 2: Graphical Representation of the Velocity Lookup Table

Velocity Mapping Examples

The following two tables are used for the following examples to show how the dwell tick to velocity mapping is performed.

Velocity Interval Table
Index Interval[0] Interval[1] Interval[2] … Interval[123] Interval[124] Interval[125] Interval[126]
Output 11 15 20 … 470 490 510 550
Velocity Look Up Table
Index LUT[0] LUT[1] LUT[2] … LUT[123] LUT[124] LUT[125] LUT[126] LUT[127]
Output 127 126 125 … 5 4 3 2 1

Example 1

A Note On event was triggered on Key 1 on board 1 with a recorded dwell tick value of 500. The dwell tick value is processed with the velocity interval table to determine the region index. The dwell tick value is compared to each Interval [i] value. Since the dwell tick value of the key is 500 and lies between [Interval [124]: Interval [125]], the region index is region 125.

The region index is then inputted into the velocity look up table. The output of LUT [125] is 3.

The final MIDI velocity for the Note event triggered by board 1 key 1 is 3.

Example 2

A Note On event was triggered on Key 3 on board 1 with a recorded dwell tick value of 558. The dwell tick value is processed with the velocity interval table to determine the region index. The dwell tick value is compared to each Interval [i] value. Since the dwell tick value of the key is 558 is above Interval [126], the region index is 127.

The region index is then inputted into the velocity look up table. The output of LUT [127] is 1.

The final MIDI velocity for the Note event triggered by board 1 key 3 is 1.
